headings.text: The Ingenix scandal births FAIR Health
"Bitter Pill" makes billing a national story
Hospital Price Transparency rule takes effect
The Price of Not Knowing the Price
Payers join in: Transparency in Coverage
The first fines land in Georgia
What the 2025 Penalty Wave Means for Hospitals
Compliance is still a moving target
The Current State of Hospital Price Transparency
What happens if a hospital does not comply with price transparency rules?
When did healthcare price transparency become law?

pages.bodyText: A Visual History What is healthcareprice transparency? For nearly a century, the price of American healthcare was a secret — locked in chargemasters and negotiated behind closed doors. Then, law by law and fine by fine, the prices came out. This is the story of how it happened. Scroll the timeline Part One The Opaque Era For most of the last century, Americans had no realistic way to learn what a hospital visit would cost before the bill arrived. Prices existed — they were just hidden. visibility_off 1930s Insurance hides the price tag Before the Great Depression, most American healthcare was paid in cash — and patients cared deeply about prices. As private health insurance spread from the 1930s onward, a third party stepped between patients and providers, and the actual price of care slowly disappeared from view. receipt_long 1950s–90s The chargemaster takes over Hospitals built sprawling internal price lists called "chargemasters" — tens of thousands of line items, set internally, varying wildly between facilities, and often many times the actual cost of an item. They were never designed for patients to read, and almost no one outside the billing office ever saw one. gavel 2003 California's Payers' Bill of Rights California enacted AB 1627, one of the first laws in the country requiring hospitals to file and disclose their chargemasters and prices for common procedures. It proved a state could force price lists into the open — even if the lists themselves were nearly impossible for consumers to use. travel_explore 2007 New Hampshire launches HealthCost Building on one of the nation’s first all-payer claims databases (mandated in 2003), the New Hampshire Insurance Department launched HealthCost — the first state website where consumers could compare what insurers actually paid for about 30 common services. Real paid amounts, not list prices, for the first time. balance 2009 The Ingenix scandal births FAIR Health A New York Attorney General investigation found that Ingenix, a UnitedHealth subsidiary used industry-wide to set "usual and customary" out-of-network rates, had skewed those rates downward — shifting costs onto consumers. The settlement funded FAIR Health, an independent nonprofit that opened billions of claims to public benchmarking. Part Two The Regulatory Wave Washington entered the fight. Over one decade, price transparency went from a single sentence in the Affordable Care Act to sweeping federal rules covering every hospital and health plan in the country. description 2010 March 23, 2010 The ACA plants the seed — §2718(e) Buried in the Affordable Care Act, Section 2718(e) of the Public Health Service Act required every U.S. hospital to establish, update, and publish a list of its standard charges each year. The sentence sat largely dormant for nearly a decade — but it became the legal foundation for everything that followed. newspaper 2013 February 2013 "Bitter Pill" makes billing a national story Steven Brill’s 24,000-word Time cover story — the first time the magazine devoted its entire feature section to a single article — dissected real hospital bills line by line and dragged the chargemaster into public consciousness. Price opacity became a mainstream outrage, not an industry quirk. history_edu 2019 June 24, 2019 Executive Order 13877 The first Trump administration signed "Improving Price and Quality Transparency in American Healthcare," directing HHS to make hospitals and insurers reveal real negotiated prices. That November, CMS finalized the Hospital Price Transparency rule — and hospitals sued to stop it. The courts sided with CMS. folder_open 2021 January 1, 2021 Hospital Price Transparency rule takes effect Every U.S. hospital was now required to publish a machine-readable file (MRF) of all standard charges — gross charges, discounted cash prices, payer-specific negotiated rates, and de-identified min/max — plus a consumer-friendly display of 300 shoppable services. Negotiated rates, long treated as trade secrets, were publicly disclosed on a national scale for the first time. api API & Data Delivery Hospital MRFs are massive and messy. SumHealth ingests and normalizes them from 5,000+ hospitals into clean, queryable data. Learn more arrow_forward shield 2022 January 1, 2022 The No Surprises Act arrives Signed in December 2020 and effective for plan years starting January 1, 2022, the No Surprises Act banned most surprise out-of-network "balance bills" — for emergency care, out-of-network providers at in-network facilities, and air ambulances — and gave uninsured patients the right to a good-faith cost estimate. auto_awesome TrueCharge AI Drop a CMS-1500 or UB-04 bill and let our AI reprice it instantly. Closes chargemaster gaps and ensures every service is reimbursed accurately. Learn more arrow_forward Drop your bill here PDF UB-04 Blog Post The Price of Not Knowing the Price Why paying cash can beat insurance — and how real hospital prices change the math for millions of patients. Read more cloud_upload 2022 July 1, 2022 Payers join in: Transparency in Coverage The Transparency in Coverage rule required health plans to publish machine-readable files of every in-network negotiated rate and historical out-of-network allowed amount. The payer files dwarfed the hospital data — refreshed monthly, measured in terabytes, and spanning most of the commercially insured market. hub Payer Data SumHealth processes negotiated-rate files from 200+ payers into market-ready intelligence. Learn more arrow_forward Brief Transparency in Coverage: A 5-Minute Briefing The TiC rule’s core requirements, who it applies to, and why the data matters — in five minutes. Read more Part Three The Enforcement Era Rules only matter if someone enforces them. Penalties grew teeth, the first fines landed, and the requirements themselves kept tightening. trending_up 2022 January 2022 Penalties get real CMS raised the maximum penalty for non-compliant hospitals from a flat $300 per day to as much as $5,500 per day for the largest facilities — putting a full year of non-compliance at over $2 million per hospital. gavel 2022 June 7, 2022 The first fines land in Georgia CMS issued its first-ever civil monetary penalties: $883,180 against Northside Hospital Atlanta and $214,320 against Northside Hospital Cherokee — nearly $1.1 million combined — after the hospitals ignored warning letters and corrective action requests. The message: the rule would be enforced. verified_user Compliance Services SumHealth helps hospitals and payers keep their transparency files complete, accurate, and audit-ready. Learn more arrow_forward rule 2024 January 1, 2024 CMS standardizes the files The CY 2024 OPPS final rule began phasing in stricter requirements: a required CMS template layout for MRFs, a "Price Transparency" link in every hospital website footer, a machine-readable .txt file in the site root, and — from July 1, 2024 — an executive affirmation that the data is true and complete. campaign 2025 February 25, 2025 Executive Order 14221 doubles down A new executive order — "Making America Healthy Again by Empowering Patients with Clear, Accurate, and Actionable Healthcare Pricing Information" — directed agencies to require actual prices rather than estimates, standardize data across hospitals and plans, and step up enforcement against both. speed 2025 Through 2025 Enforcement accelerates CMS sharply picked up the pace, fining ten hospitals in 2025 alone after just three in 2024 — bringing total civil monetary penalties to more than two dozen hospitals since enforcement began, with more warning letters and corrective action requests in the pipeline. Insight What the 2025 Penalty Wave Means for Hospitals CMS enforcement patterns in 2025 — expanded audits, accelerated penalties, and what hospitals should do now. Read more Part Four Today & Tomorrow The data is public. The work now is making it usable — turning millions of raw price files into decisions patients, providers, employers, and payers can actually act on. query_stats Now Compliance is still a moving target Most hospitals now post a machine-readable file, but independent reviews disagree on how many are fully compliant — recent estimates range from roughly a fifth of hospitals (PatientRightsAdvocate.org) to about two-thirds (an HHS OIG audit), depending on how strictly the rules are read. The gap between "posted" and "usable" is where the next chapter is being written. Blog Post The Current State of Hospital Price Transparency Where compliance really stands, what the newest rules require, and what comes next for hospitals and patients. Read more insights Next From transparency to intelligence Raw transparency data is measured in terabytes and formatted a hundred different ways. The frontier now is normalization, benchmarking, and delivery — making every negotiated rate in America as easy to look up as a flight price. That’s the future SumHealth is building. bar_chart Benchmarks Proprietary benchmarks that define your market position instantly. A single source of truth across payer and hospital data for finance, ops, and contracting teams. Learn more arrow_forward Quick Answers Price transparency, in plain English What is healthcare price transparency? Healthcare price transparency is the requirement that hospitals and health insurers publicly disclose the actual prices of care — including negotiated rates, cash prices, and standard charges — so patients and purchasers can compare costs before receiving care. In the U.S. it is anchored by the CMS Hospital Price Transparency rule (effective January 1, 2021) and the Transparency in Coverage rule for health plans (machine-readable files effective July 1, 2022). What is a machine-readable file (MRF)? A machine-readable file is a structured data file (typically JSON or CSV) that hospitals and health plans must publish containing their standard charges or negotiated rates. Hospital MRFs list gross charges, discounted cash prices, and payer-specific negotiated rates; payer MRFs list in-network negotiated rates and out-of-network allowed amounts for covered items and services. What happens if a hospital does not comply with price transparency rules? CMS can issue warning letters, require corrective action plans, and impose civil monetary penalties of up to $5,500 per day for the largest hospitals — over $2 million per year of non-compliance. CMS issued its first fines in June 2022 to two Georgia hospitals totaling nearly $1.1 million, and enforcement has accelerated since. When did healthcare price transparency become law? The foundation was laid in 2010 by Section 2718(e) of the Affordable Care Act, which required hospitals to publish standard charges. A 2019 executive order led CMS to finalize the Hospital Price Transparency rule, effective January 1, 2021, followed by the No Surprises Act (January 1, 2022) and the Transparency in Coverage rule for payers (July 1, 2022).

pages.bodyText: Legal Privacy Policy Effective date: December 27, 2023 On this page What We Collect How We Use It Information Sharing Retention Your Choices Your Rights Children Third-Party Links Security Policy Changes Contact Us Welcome to the SumHealth website (the "Site"). SumHealth, Inc. ("SumHealth," "we," "us," or "our") is a healthcare data software-as-a-service company offering a range of solutions. This privacy policy outlines how we handle the personal information you may provide to us during your interaction with our services. Please review this Privacy Policy carefully before using our services. By accessing the Site or using our services, you agree to the practices described in this Privacy Policy. What Information We Collect Personal Information You Provide: We collect personally identifiable information from you, including your name, email address, phone number, and mailing/billing addresses when you create an account, participate in the Community, communicate with our support teams, or fill out forms on our Site. Non-Personally Identifying Information: When you interact with our services, we collect non-personally identifying information such as device information (manufacturer, model, operating system, IP address), usage information, user experience information, and location information. Social Media Information: If you interact with us on social media platforms, we may receive personal information based on your settings, such as contact details. How We Use the Information We Collect Your personal information is used for the following purposes: Service Delivery — To provide, operate, and maintain our services. Communication — To respond to inquiries, send service-related notices, and provide customer support. Service Improvement — To understand how our services are used and to improve them. Compliance and Protection — To comply with legal obligations and protect the rights of SumHealth and our users. Marketing and Advertising — To send promotional communications, subject to your choices described below. We process data on behalf of our customers to provide the Solution. Personal Information Sharing We do not sell, rent, license, or lease your personal information to third parties. In certain circumstances, we may share personal information with: Service Providers — Third parties that assist us in operating our website and services. Professional Advisors — Lawyers, auditors, and other advisors as necessary. Business Partners — Partners assisting with business operations or a transaction, such as a merger or acquisition. Personal Information Retention We retain personal information for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Privacy Policy, as required by law, or while we have a legitimate business need to do so. Your Choices You can take the following steps to control how your information is used: Account Information — You may update your account information at any time by logging into your account. Marketing Communications — You may opt out of marketing emails by clicking "unsubscribe" in any marketing message or by contacting us directly. Online Tracking — You may limit certain forms of online tracking through your browser settings or the opt-out mechanisms described below. Your Rights You have rights with respect to your personal information, including the right to access, delete, correct, and port your data. To exercise these rights, please contact us at contact@sumhealth.org. Users in California and the European Union may have additional rights under applicable law, including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Please contact us for more information about how to exercise your rights under those frameworks. Children Our Service is not directed to children under the age of 18, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If we learn that we have collected personal information from a child under 18, we will take steps to delete that information promptly. Links to Other Websites The Service may contain links to other websites not operated or controlled by SumHealth. Information shared on third-party sites is governed by their own privacy policies, and we are not responsible for their privacy practices. We encourage you to review the privacy policy of any third-party site you visit. Security We implement technical, organizational, and physical safeguards designed to protect the personal information we collect. Our security practices align with industry standards. However, no method of transmission over the Internet or electronic storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. Changes to the Privacy Policy We may change this Privacy Policy at any time. When we do, we will revise the "Effective date" at the top of this page. By continuing to use our Service after an update, you agree to the revised Privacy Policy. We encourage you to review this page periodically. Contact Us For questions about our Privacy Policy or information practices, please contact us at: contact@sumhealth.org When you visit or log in to our website, cookies and similar technologies may be used by our online data partners or vendors to associate these activities with other personal information they or others have about you, including by association with your email. We (or service providers on our behalf) may then send communications and marketing to these email addresses. You may opt out of receiving this advertising by visiting https://app.retention.com/optout.

headings.text: Healthcare Price Transparency Compliance — Done Right
CMS Is Enforcing. The Penalties Are Real.
The CMS Price Transparency Rule at a Glance
We've Processed Hospital MRFs Nationwide. We Know What Good Looks Like.
Don't Wait for CMS to Come Knocking

pages.bodyText: Compliance Healthcare Price Transparency Compliance — Done Right CMS enforcement is escalating. SumHealth gives hospitals and health systems the tools and expertise to achieve compliance, stay audit-ready, and protect against civil monetary penalties. Get a Compliance Assessment The Stakes CMS Is Enforcing. The Penalties Are Real. The Hospital Price Transparency Rule requires hospitals to publish machine-readable files and consumer-friendly displays for all standard charges. Non-compliant hospitals face civil monetary penalties up to $2 million per year — and CMS is actively issuing warning letters and enforcement actions. $300/day Penalty rate for hospitals under 30 beds $10/day Per bed for larger hospitals (up to $5,500/day) $2M/yr Maximum annual civil monetary penalty Our Services End-to-End Compliance Support search Compliance Audit & Gap Analysis We review your existing MRF files and consumer-facing displays against the current CMS requirements — identifying every gap before CMS does. build_circle MRF File Generation & Remediation We generate or remediate your machine-readable files to meet the CMS schema requirements — including all required data elements for every standard charge. monitor_heart Ongoing Compliance Monitoring Automated checks that flag issues as your charge data changes — so your files stay compliant 365 days a year, not just at implementation. description Consumer-Facing Display A compliant, user-friendly shoppable services display embedded on your hospital website — meeting the plain-language and searchability requirements. policy Enforcement Response Support Received a CMS warning letter or corrective action plan request? We provide expert support to draft your response and achieve compliance fast. school Staff Training & Documentation We train your revenue cycle and compliance teams on the requirements, establish internal governance, and document your compliance program. What's Required The CMS Price Transparency Rule at a Glance The Hospital Price Transparency Rule took effect January 1, 2021 and has been updated with increasing stringency since. Here's what every hospital must have in place: Machine-Readable File (MRF) A comprehensive, publicly available file with all standard charges — including gross charges, discounted cash prices, payer-specific negotiated rates, and de-identified min/max rates. Consumer-Friendly Display A searchable, plain-language display of at least 300 shoppable services on your public website — accessible without registration or login. Schema Compliance Files must conform to the CMS Technical Implementation Guide — specific JSON/CSV schema, required fields, and encoding standards that are updated periodically. Ongoing Accuracy Files must be updated at least annually or whenever rates change materially. Stale or inaccurate data is itself a compliance violation. Why SumHealth We've Processed Hospital MRFs Nationwide. We Know What Good Looks Like. database Nationwide Data Coverage SumHealth processes hospital MRF files from across the country. We've seen the schema errors, edge cases, and enforcement patterns that trip hospitals up. gavel Enforcement Intelligence We monitor CMS enforcement activity and rule updates in real time — so your compliance posture evolves as the regulatory environment does. speed Fast Time to Compliance Our automated tooling and expert team get most hospitals to full compliance within 30–60 days — significantly faster than internal remediation efforts. support_agent Ongoing Partnership We don't disappear after implementation. Continuous monitoring, annual updates, and responsive support keep you compliant year-round. Who It's For Is Your Hospital at Risk? CMS has identified thousands of non-compliant hospitals. If any of the following apply to your organization, it's time to act. Request a Free Compliance Review You've received a CMS warning letter or corrective action plan request Your MRF was published more than 12 months ago without updates You're unsure if your file meets the current CMS schema requirements Your consumer-facing shoppable services display is missing or incomplete You're part of a health system and haven't audited all member hospitals No one internally owns compliance monitoring on an ongoing basis Don't Wait for CMS to Come Knocking Our compliance team will review your current status and give you a clear picture of where you stand — at no cost. From there, we'll build a remediation plan that fits your timeline and budget. Request Your Free Compliance Review

When you self-insure, every inflated charge and over-negotiated rate comes straight out of your bottom line, and your employees' paychecks. Yet most employers can't see what their plan is actually paying versus fair market rates. SumHealth changes that. Book a Demo Explore TrueCharge AI Claim-level benchmarks Overcharge detection HIPAA secure corporate_fare Coverage 5,000+ Hospitals priced for your plan All 50 states The challenge You pay the bill, but you can't see the price Self-funded plans bear 100% of claim costs, yet the prices behind those claims are buried in network contracts and itemized bills no one audits against the market. receipt_long Overcharges hit your plan directly Inflated facility fees and marked-up line items flow straight through to your plan spend. Without repricing, you pay them without ever knowing. savings Rising costs, fewer levers Premiums and claim costs climb every year. Shifting cost to employees has limits. headings.text: Your Labs Are Normal. Your Body Says Otherwise.
Tell us what you are working on.
Grow your practice with patients seeking personalized care.
You know something feels off.Let’s find out why.
You're in. Here is what happens next.

pages.bodyText: SumHealth Wellness Your Labs Are Normal. Your Body Says Otherwise. SumHealth Wellness connects you with an independent, licensed provider for personalized care built around your goals, your health, and your individual needs. Providers may evaluate hormones, metabolism, nutrition, lifestyle, and other factors to develop a plan that fits you, including personalized and compounded treatment options when appropriate. Schedule consultation How it works Look beyond “normal” lab results Trusted, independent providers Currently available in NC Cash pay Direct, transparent pricing No insurance No claims or middlemen No referrals Direct access to providers Telehealth may be available through independent practices in North Carolina. A Different Standard Why this is different No insurance, no gatekeeping Insurance decides what gets covered, which means it decides what gets discussed. Paying directly removes the middleman. You and the provider decide what to test and what to try, without waiting on an authorization. Time to actually look A typical primary care visit runs 15 minutes. This is not that. Comprehensive labs, a real intake, and a provider who reads the results with you instead of sending a portal message that says "all normal." Built around how you feel Being outside the disease range is not the same as feeling good. The focus here is energy, sleep, body composition, mood, and drive, measured against your own baseline. You’re in the right place if: Have symptoms your labs have not explained Are willing to pay directly for care that insurance will not cover Want data and a plan, not a supplement subscription Are 18 or older and live in North Carolina Schedule consultation Clinical Focus What gets covered Schedule consultation Hormone health Testosterone, thyroid, cortisol, and perimenopause. Full panels, evaluated by a provider who treats hormones as a system and not a single number on a lab slip. Metabolic health and weight Insulin resistance, lipids, inflammation, and body composition. Where medication is clinically appropriate, the provider will discuss the FDA approved options with you. Energy, sleep, and recovery The complaints that get dismissed most often, taken seriously and worked up properly. Longevity and advanced therapies An honest read on what the evidence supports, what is still speculative, and what is legally available right now. We will tell you when the answer is "not yet." The Process How it works Schedule consultation 1 Tell us what you are working on. Two minutes, four questions. No medical history required at this stage. 2 Get matched. We introduce you to an independent licensed provider who practices in your state. They review your information and reach out directly. 3 Get evaluated. Comprehensive labs and a real conversation. The provider determines what, if anything, is appropriate for you. 4 Get managed. If treatment makes sense, the provider manages it and adjusts over time. Any medication is dispensed by a licensed pharmacy. All clinical decisions, including whether any treatment or medication is appropriate, are made solely by the licensed provider after evaluating you. SumHealth does not provide medical care and does not prescribe. For Clinicians Grow your practice with patients seeking personalized care. Join the SumHealth Wellness provider network and get connected with people actively looking for personalized, functional, and integrative care. We send qualified patient leads your way, so you can spend less time marketing and more time doing what you do best: helping people get better. Interested in receiving patient referrals? Join our network The Details Have Questions? We've Got Answers Schedule consultation Who is this not a fit for? This is not a fit if you: Are looking for a specific drug and a prescription with no evaluationNeed urgent or emergency careAre hoping to bill insurance for the visitsWant a guarantee before anyone has looked at your labs That last one is not us being difficult. A provider who will promise you a prescription before evaluating you is not a provider you want. Will I get a prescription? Only if an independent licensed provider evaluates you and determines it is appropriate. Nothing is guaranteed, and any provider promising otherwise is a red flag. How much does it cost? This is a cash pay service. The provider's practice sets its own pricing and bills you directly. SumHealth does not set prices and does not take a share of what you pay for care. We do not bill insurance. No claims, no deductibles, no surprise explanation of benefits six weeks later. You will know the cost before anything happens.You may be able to use HSA/FSA. Many patients do. Check with your plan administrator, since rules vary.Some labs may be covered. If you choose to run them through your own insurance plan, the provider can talk you through that option during evaluation. Why no insurance? Insurance coverage drives what gets tested and discussed. Cash pay keeps that decision between you and your provider. It also means no prior authorization delays. Is this legitimate telehealth? If you are matched for telehealth care, the independent practice is responsible for confirming that its licensed clinician can legally care for you in North Carolina. Who sees my information? What you submit goes to SumHealth and to the independent medical practice we introduce you to, and only with your explicit consent. We do not sell your information. SumHealth is a healthcare pricing data company and does not provide medical care, prescribe, or dispense medication. Medical services are provided by an independent licensed practice that is solely responsible for all clinical decisions. SumHealth may receive a fixed fee for this introduction; the fee does not vary with what is prescribed or dispensed and does not affect SumHealth pricing data. This is a cash pay service and insurance is not billed. Submitting this form does not create a physician patient relationship or guarantee treatment. Compounded medications are not FDA approved. × You know something feels off.Let’s find out why. Four questions. No medical history, no credit card. SumHealth will review your information to see whether an independent licensed practice may be a fit. First name * Phone * Email * State * Select your state... North Carolina What are you focused on? (Select up to 2) * Hormone health Metabolic health and weight Energy, sleep, and recovery Longevity and advanced therapies General functional medicine Not sure yet Comfortable with cash pay in the $150 to $400 per month range? Select... Yes Depends on the plan No I am 18 or older and a US resident. * I understand this is a cash pay service, that insurance is not billed, and that SumHealth does not provide medical care, prescribe medication, or guarantee that any treatment will be appropriate for me. * I agree that SumHealth may share my name, email, phone, and state with an independent medical practice so they can contact me about a consultation. I can withdraw this consent at any time by emailing privacy@sumhealth.org. * I agree to receive email and text messages from SumHealth and from the practice about this program. Message frequency varies, message and data rates may apply, reply STOP to opt out. * Send me the SumHealth Wellness newsletter. See if I'm a fit We do not sell your information. Privacy Notice. Terms. You're in. Here is what happens next. SumHealth will review your information, and an independent licensed practice may contact you to discuss next steps (usually within one business day by phone). We do not promise a prescription, treatment, exact response time, or guaranteed match. × Join Our Provider Community Great care starts with great clinicians. We’re building relationships with exceptional independent providers who look at the whole person, not just a diagnosis or lab result. We’re especially interested in clinicians practicing functional medicine, integrative medicine, nutrition, and other personalized approaches who bring deep expertise, curiosity, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping their patients feel their best. If that sounds like you, fill out the form below. Full name * Work email * Phone * Practice or organization * Specialty / Credentials * Licensed states * I consent to SumHealth contacting me about network opportunities and storing my application data in accordance with the Privacy Policy. * Submit inquiry We do not sell your information. Privacy Notice. Application received. Thank you for your interest. Our team will review your details and reach out to discuss next steps.

pages.bodyText: Partner with SumHealth Your members are shopping for care with a blindfold on. Cash prices for the same MRI, blood panel, or outpatient procedure can vary several times over from one facility to the next, and almost nobody sees the difference until the bill arrives. We built the tool that shows them. We'll put your name on it. Request a partner demo See how white label works MRI Northside Imaging Center 2.1 mi · MRI, lumbar, no contrast $389 Lowest cash price Lakeview Radiology 4.8 mi · MRI, lumbar, no contrast $540 County General Hospital 3.2 mi · MRI, lumbar, no contrast $1,760 Example prices for illustration The gap Cash-pay members already have the incentive. They're missing the tool. Health shares, RBP plans, ICHRA stipends, fixed-indemnity coverage: the structures are different, but the member's position is the same. Pay first, out of pocket, with no negotiated rate behind them. money_off No negotiated rate Members pay the facility's cash rate directly, before sharing, reimbursement, or a stipend applies. There's no insurer in the middle to absorb the difference. search_off No usable pricing Most imaging centers, labs, and surgery centers don't publish real self-pay prices anywhere a member could find and compare them before booking. explore_off High intent, no destination These members are already motivated shoppers. Right now they're calling around or guessing. Nobody is handing them a comparison. The product A member searches once. We show them who's cheapest. Search by procedure and location. See verified cash prices across imaging centers, labs, and outpatient surgery centers, ranked and ready to book. White label Your brand up front. Our engine underneath. Members see your logo, your colors, your domain. We handle the provider data, price verification, and search infrastructure behind it, updated continuously, without any work on your end. palette Your branding Logo, color palette, and tone across every screen a member sees. language Your domain Embedded in your member portal or hosted at a subdomain of your choice. forum Your member communications The tool sits inside the touchpoints members already trust. database Our data pipeline Sourced, verified, and refreshed continuously, invisible to the member. passkey Your login flow SSO support so members access the tool from your portal without a separate account, or standalone access if that is simpler for your setup. Who it's for Built for organizations whose members already pay cash. If your members shop, reimburse, or share costs directly, this fits your model. diversity_3 Health Sharing Ministries Members cover costs out of pocket up to their unshared amount, with no negotiated rate behind them. price_check Reference-Based Pricing Administrators Plans built around a Medicare multiple need to show members where to find care near that target price. work ICHRA & QSEHRA Platforms Employees spending a fixed allowance need to know the real cost before they spend it. stethoscope Direct Primary Care Networks Member physicians order labs and imaging constantly and need a reliable place to send patients for cash pricing. savings HSA & FSA Platforms Account holders spending their own tax-advantaged dollars benefit from shopping before they spend. gavel Bill Advocates & Fixed-Indemnity Carriers A pre-service price check complements post-service negotiation and fixed-payout coverage alike. Getting started Three steps to launch. 1 Connect We integrate however fits your stack: embedded in your member portal, through our API, or with SSO so members move between your platform and the tool without a separate login. 2 Brand it Send your logo and colors. We apply your identity across the member-facing experience. 3 Launch Go live to your members. We keep the pricing data current, with no ongoing work required from your team. Ready to give your members a price they can trust? Tell us a bit about your organization and member base. We'll walk through a live demo and what a white-label build would look like for you. # SumHealth

> SumHealth provides healthcare price transparency data, tools, and APIs — including hospital and payer negotiated rate pricing, rate benchmarking, bill repricing, and compliance analytics — used by patients, providers, payers, employers, brokers, consultants, developers, and researchers.

Canonical domain: https://sumhealth.org

This file lists the primary, canonical URLs on sumhealth.org that AI systems and crawlers should prioritize when summarizing or citing this site. Some routes below are legacy aliases or redirects retained for backward compatibility; always prefer and cite the canonical destination, not the alias.

## Products

- [BenchMarks](https://sumhealth.org/benchmarks): Healthcare pricing benchmark insights.

- Operated by SumHealth.
- Free for individual searches; no account, email address, or credit card is required.
- Covers 5,000+ hospitals across all 50 states, plus a growing set of provider-submitted cash prices.
- Source data includes hospital Machine-Readable Files and provider-submitted cash prices.
- The searchable dataset is refreshed monthly as new source data becomes available.
- Published prices are comparison information, not guaranteed estimates; users should confirm the complete cash price with the hospital or provider before care.
